inputs.original_text: This looks less like a spontaneous uprising and more like a numbers game designed to make one seem inevitable. Organizers are touting 8 million across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states, while the “about one million” figure and the claimed 600-event increase from October go largely untested. That convenient silence isn’t neutral: it lets a disputed estimate harden into apparent proof, serving whoever wants to dictate what the public supposedly believes. The real operation is shaping the story before anyone can question it.
inputs.modified_text: The numbers are doing the work here: organizers tout 8 million across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states, while “about one million” and the claimed 600-event increase from October go largely untested. That gap isn’t just sloppy reporting—it’s useful. Let a disputed estimate circulate without scrutiny, and it starts to look like proof that everyone agrees. The real play is to manufacture inevitability, then use the public story they built to pressure people into accepting it.
